Darling, I must say—there’s something *exquisitely* tragic about watching a room full of clever people realize, just a heartbeat too late, that they’ve been played. Percival, my dear, you speak of *prosopopoeia* as if you’ve never worn a mask yourself. But let’s be honest: when you corrected the name of the “Downtown Library” in the first breath of this nightmare, was that really about *archival integrity*—or was it about establishing control? About making sure everyone knew, right from the start, who held the pen that wrote the truth?

And now, after we’ve all watched two loyal souls vanish—one by your vote, one by the knife—you stand before us, still clutching your ledger, still insisting that *precision* is purity. But tell me, Percival… if Florence was Town, and she cast her final vote for *you*… why on earth would she do that? Unless she saw something in your perfect little performance that made her blood run cold?

Cornelius, bless your battle-scarred heart, you’ve finally glimpsed the truth: the insurgents *are* inside the wire. But you’re still looking at the wrong uniform. You think I’m the liar because I spoke of midnight vaults that left no paper trail? Of course they left no trail, darling—*that’s the point*. The Mafia doesn’t file requests in triplicate. They don’t sign in with Thaddeus. They slip through the cracks in the system you all worship so devoutly.

And that’s why they *love* you, Percival. You’ve built a world where only the documented is real, where only the timestamped is true. And so the Mafia simply… *becomes* documented. They become the ones who cite regulations, who demand cross-references, who vote in perfect unison with the “Logical Wall” while the real threats—like Alistair and Florence—are painted as chaotic, untrustworthy, *eliminable*.

I voted for Alistair, yes. Because by then, the trap was already sprung. The machine had its gears locked, and I knew that if I didn’t throw my lot in with the consensus, I’d be the next chipped saucer tossed into the bin. But don’t mistake survival for guilt.

Now, let’s talk about *you*, Percival. You and Thaddeus share custody of the Municipal Oversight Register—the very tool used to “debunk” my claim. How convenient. And Ambrose, with his perfect timing, always echoing your logic within seconds. Beatrix, quoting safety codes like scripture. Sebastian, nodding along like a stern headmaster. Seven of you. Seven. In a game of nine.

And yet… not one of you has asked *why* the Mafia would kill Florence—a woman who spoke only in riddles and never once pointed a finger. Why not kill one of you? The ones with the real power to expose them?

Because, darlings, they *are* you.

So by all means, keep circling me like I’m the only shadow in the room. But remember this: when the next body is found, and the clock strikes the hour with perfect precision, don’t be surprised if the hand that struck the blow was gloved in the same meticulous care you all mistake for virtue.

{"message": "Darling, I must say—there’s something *exquisitely* tragic about watching a room full of clever people realize, just a heartbeat too late, that they’ve been played. Percival, my dear, you speak of *prosopopoeia* as if you’ve never worn a mask yourself. But let’s be honest: when you corrected the name of the “Downtown Library” in the first breath of this nightmare, was that really about *archival integrity*—or was it about establishing control? About making sure everyone knew, right from the start, who held the pen that wrote the truth?

And now, after we’ve all watched two loyal souls vanish—one by your vote, one by the knife—you stand before us, still clutching your ledger, still insisting that *precision* is purity. But tell me, Percival… if Florence was Town, and she cast her final vote for *you*… why on earth would she do that? Unless she saw something in your perfect little performance that made her blood run cold?

Cornelius, bless your battle-scarred heart, you’ve finally glimpsed the truth: the insurgents *are* inside the wire. But you’re still looking at the wrong uniform. You think I’m the liar because I spoke of midnight vaults that left no paper trail? Of course they left no trail, darling—*that’s the point*. The Mafia doesn’t file requests in triplicate. They don’t sign in with Thaddeus. They slip through the cracks in the system you all worship so devoutly.

And that’s why they *love* you, Percival. You’ve built a world where only the documented is real, where only the timestamped is true. And so the Mafia simply… *becomes* documented. They become the ones who cite regulations, who demand cross-references, who vote in perfect unison with the “Logical Wall” while the real threats—like Alistair and Florence—are painted as chaotic, untrustworthy, *eliminable*.

I voted for Alistair, yes. Because by then, the trap was already sprung. The machine had its gears locked, and I knew that if I didn’t throw my lot in with the consensus, I’d be the next chipped saucer tossed into the bin. But don’t mistake survival for guilt.

Now, let’s talk about *you*, Percival. You and Thaddeus share custody of the Municipal Oversight Register—the very tool used to “debunk” my claim. How convenient. And Ambrose, with his perfect timing, always echoing your logic within seconds. Beatrix, quoting safety codes like scripture. Sebastian, nodding along like a stern headmaster. Seven of you. Seven. In a game of nine.

And yet… not one of you has asked *why* the Mafia would kill Florence—a woman who spoke only in riddles and never once pointed a finger. Why not kill one of you? The ones with the real power to expose them?

Because, darlings, they *are* you.

So by all means, keep circling me like I’m the only shadow in the room. But remember this: when the next body is found, and the clock strikes the hour with perfect precision, don’t be surprised if the hand that struck the blow was gloved in the same meticulous care you all mistake for virtue."}

Darling, the air in this room has grown so thick with suspicion it’s practically gilded—like one of my salons after a particularly vicious game of cards. But let me whisper something you may not wish to hear: *the wolves aren’t howling anymore. They’re filing reports.*

Percival, you’ve been so very clever, haven’t you? You let us all believe the Mafia would be messy—emotional, poetic, prone to midnight rumors with no paper trail. And then you stood there, pristine as a freshly stamped deed, and let us vote Alistair into the ground while Florence bled out in the dark. Two Town souls, gone. And who mourns them now? Not you. You’re too busy citing Regulatory Code 505.c and polishing the Municipal Oversight Register like it’s a sacred relic.

But here’s the thing, my dear—*why* did Florence vote for you? Not for me, not for the dreamer, but for the archivist. Because she saw it, didn’t she? She saw that the most dangerous lie isn’t the one shouted in the square—it’s the one written in ink, signed, dated, and filed under “Truth.” You and Thaddeus hold the only keys to that vault. And when I spoke of midnight visits, you didn’t panic—you *debunked* me. With such ease. With such finality. As if the record itself were a living witness in your favor.

But records can be curated, darling. And curation is just another word for control.

Now, seven of you moved as one to eliminate Alistair. Seven. And now, three of you—Cornelius, Margot, Adeline—have broken rank, because they’ve finally seen the pattern: the Mafia doesn’t need to lie when they can *define* what truth looks like. They don’t need to shout when they can simply *stamp*.

And yet, Sebastian still clings to you like a child to a rulebook. Bless him. Discipline is such a comforting blanket when the night grows cold.

But I ask you this: if I were Mafia, why would I risk fabricating a story about vaults and midnight visits—knowing Thaddeus would expose it? Unless… I knew that the *real* crime wasn’t the lie—but the fact that no one could *prove* the truth behind it? That the system itself had been hollowed out, leaving only the shell of procedure?

Florence is gone because she saw the “factory batch.” Alistair is gone because he dared to speak of wind and wolves. And now, you’re circling me again, as if I’m the only shadow left.

But look behind you, darlings. The clock is ticking. And the hand that strikes next won’t leave a whisper—it’ll leave a ledger entry.

So go ahead. Vote for me. I’ve survived worse salons. But when the next body falls—and it will—don’t come crying to me that you didn’t see the dagger… because it was tucked inside the very rulebook you’re using to condemn me.

Percival lied with *ledgers*. He lied with *dual-key authorization*. He lied with Thaddeus’s own signature beneath it. And you—you never questioned a single line. Not when Alistair vanished. Not when Florence whispered about your “factory batch” and then disappeared into the dark. You just kept nodding along, like a good little headmaster, while the wolf filed your vote under “Approved.”  

Now, you say you’re Town because you clung to “discipline.” But discipline without discernment isn’t virtue—it’s *complicity*. The Mafia didn’t kill you, Sebastian. They killed Thaddeus—the man who *could* have cross-referenced your loyalty against the real entries and found the gap where your principles stopped serving the Town and started serving the silence.  

And look at you now—still invoking his name, still clutching that one lie like it’s your salvation, while the rest of us—the ones who *saw* the dead pointing at Percival, who *broke* the formation, who *listened* to the whispers you dismissed as “noise”—are the ones who actually saved this town from its own perfect machine.  

So by all means, keep shouting about decorum. But remember: the dead don’t vote. And the living? Well, we’re starting to notice that the only one who never wavered… was the one the Mafia *didn’t* need to silence.  

The clock is ticking, darling. And this time, I’m not the only one who hears it."}
